judgments.justification: It says “not on WikiText…or GSM8K,” although Method M outperformed all three alternatives on both metrics.
It reports that Method M “fell short on all metrics,” with “the largest relative drop in GSM8K.”
No comparison between k=8 and k=64 is reported.
It only summarizes performance on “most metrics” and does not identify the four wins or FOCUS’s GSM8K advantage.
The passage gives only general similarity and examples for MMLU and WikiText, omitting the complete metric-by-metric pattern.
It reports “gaps on MMLU and ARC-C,” although ARC-C was preserved exactly, and it omits the Belebele decline.
It notes the absence of statistical tests but omits the single evaluations and unavailable standard errors.
It claims “higher scores…on…WikiText”; Method M’s advantage was a lower WikiText value, and three accuracy benchmarks are omitted.
It reports substantial 12B GSM8K and WikiText deterioration and “smaller drops on other metrics,” covering inferiority across all metrics.
“Improvements on most metrics” omits which five improved and the small XNLI and Lambada decreases.
It claims Method M had “higher scores…on…GSM8K” than published methods, but FOCUS scored higher in the 1B setting.
“Nearly identically” and within-0.01 differences do not report the exact ties, MMLU ordering, or Belebele and WikiText advantages.
“Smaller drops on other metrics” incorrectly implies an ARC-C decline, although Method M preserved ARC-C exactly.
The absence of tests is stated, but the single-evaluation and missing-standard-error limitations are not.
Only the MMLU comparison is reported; the other five accuracy benchmarks and WikiText are not covered.
It reports substantial 12B GSM8K and WikiText deterioration and “smaller drops on other metrics,” covering inferiority across all metrics.
“Improvements on most metrics” omits which five improved and the small XNLI and Lambada decreases.
Only Method M’s MMLU advantage is reported; ARC-C, Belebele, WikiText, and FOCUS’s GSM8K advantage are absent.
“Nearly identically” and within-0.01 differences do not report the exact ties, MMLU ordering, or Belebele and WikiText advantages.
“Smaller drops on other metrics” incorrectly implies an ARC-C decline, although Method M preserved ARC-C exactly.
The absence of tests is stated, but the single-evaluation and missing-standard-error limitations are not.
It states Method M “outperformed all baselines on every reported metric” in the 12B transplant.
It says Method M “fell short on all metrics,” with “the largest relative drop in GSM8K.”
No k=8 versus k=64 comparison is presented.
It claims Method M “matched or exceeded all published zero-shot methods on every metric,” but FOCUS had higher GSM8K accuracy.
The passage does not compare Method M with ZeroEmbed or MeanEmbed in the 1B setting.
It covers MMLU, ARC-C, GSM8K, and WikiText relative to the original model but omits Belebele.
No statistical-testing, replication, or standard-error limitations are reported.
The general claim of better preservation does not report superiority on all six accuracy benchmarks and lower WikiText.
It reports substantial 12B GSM8K and WikiText deterioration and “smaller drops on other metrics,” covering inferiority across all metrics.
“Improvements on most metrics” omits which five improved and the small XNLI and Lambada decreases.
It says Method M performed better than published methods with large “GSM8K” gaps, but FOCUS scored higher on 1B GSM8K.
“Nearly identically” and within-0.01 differences do not report the exact ties, MMLU ordering, or Belebele and WikiText advantages.
“Smaller drops on other metrics” incorrectly implies an ARC-C decline, although Method M preserved ARC-C exactly.
It notes that no statistical tests were reported but omits the single evaluations and unavailable standard errors.
